title: Needless Interference
text: “Everyone, save Bow Hero-dono from Shield!”
The moment Trash made that declaration, the mages stationed around the crowd began chanting their spells.
“Yeah, yeah. Looks like reinforcements are coming. Good luck, Itsuki.”
“Whoa! N-nooooooo!?”

Father grabbed Itsuki by the scruff of the neck and used him as a shield against the rain of magic unleashed by Trash’s order. Fire first, then wind, earth, light, darkness, lightning—an entire assortment of spells, all present and accounted for. They struck one after another with heavy thuds, and Itsuki got thoroughly pummeled.
“A-aaah…”
“Whoa… Itsuki, you okay? You’re not dead, right? Fast Heal X.”
Itsuki, half-charred and twitching with various status ailments here and there, received Father’s healing.
“What are you doing!”

Crocodile Guy roared at this point. Ah, I’d thought Ren might step in, but it seemed he still hadn’t returned yet. Trash, utterly indifferent to Crocodile Guy’s fury, turned a contemptuous gaze on him and his companions and scoffed.
“Shield Hero used the cowardly tactic of poison. Therefore, this match is decided in favor of Bow Hero-dono’s victory!”
“Don’t be ridiculous! There was no such agreement beforehand! Shield Hero-sama has no means of attack, so this is a legitimate improvisation!”
Crocodile Guy’s voice echoed across the arena. Meanwhile, Father himself seemed more concerned with the groaning, agonized Itsuki.
“Itsuki, looks like they’re trying to turn this into my loss by disqualification, but can you still say this counts as your win?”
“Ugh, uuh…”
Itsuki, not yet recovered from the shock of the pain, glared through tearful eyes at Trash and the Crimson Swine before turning his gaze back to Father.
“Aultcray… if you don’t cut this out, I’ll wring your neck off myself, even if it costs me my own life!”

Crocodile Guy’s muscles bulged. I could sense the stirrings of magic. If I recalled correctly, Crocodile Guy’s magical affinity was… the same attribute as the Siltvelt envoy, or something like that. Apparently he also had an aptitude for water magic. He was working to boost his own abilities by activating his life force. And beyond that—this particular current felt close to something like ki. Word was that an attack called Power Tornado, a condensed burst of life force that could be called either spell or technique, was about to burst forth. With Crocodile Guy’s overflowing vitality, it apparently had the potential to become a devastating critical strike.
“Shion, not yet. Even defying Iwatani-sama’s orders wouldn’t make this right!”
Rabbit Guy stepped in front of Crocodile Guy to stop him.
“Don’t stop me! I’m at my limit already!”
“Well, that can’t be helped then.”
I gave Crocodile Guy a good stab with Sleep Lance VII.
“Ah!? Guuuh… I—can’t—collapse—in a situation like this—”
Hmm… quite tough, indeed. In honor of that spirit, I stabbed him again with Sleep Lance X, potent enough to knock someone out for three days.
“Guuu… still not—”

Staggering forward a few steps with bloodshot eyes, he pulled out an axe and tried to charge at Trash, but that was where Crocodile Guy’s movement finally stopped. Oh… he was sleeping standing up. That’s the thing—if this had been an attack with real lethal force, this is the sort of thing that would leave someone dead on their feet. It was astonishing how poorly the status effects had worked on him this far—a testament to just how strong his will must be. His fury on Father’s behalf, the sheer resolve to go that far—that deserved praise indeed.
“Shion… I respect that fighting spirit of yours.”

Rabbit Guy pressed his hands together, tears streaming down his face. Eventually, whatever transformation had been active on him seemed to wear off, and Crocodile Guy shifted into the form of some sort of Demi-Human that wasn’t quite a mixed-breed lizardman. The scattered, incomplete lizard-like features now had a certain unified look to them. Well, since Ren wasn’t here yet, I supposed I’d have to be the one to wrap things up.
“Now then, given this needless interference in Itsuki’s favor, I trust we can agree this counts as a disqualification loss for Itsuki’s side?”
“Bu-bhee! Bu-bu-bu-bu!”
The Crimson Swine emerged from behind Trash and seemed to be raising some sort of protest. If it had a complaint, I’d be more than happy to butcher it right here on the spot, wouldn’t I?
“The moment it cowardly cast magic while hiding among the crowd, that was proof of premeditated intent. As a Hero, I’ll pass judgment on you here and now.”
“B-bhee-hyaaaaaaa!?”
I leveled my spear sharply and approached with a look reserved for garbage, threatening it—at which point Trash stepped in between us. Oh ho, coming to die on your own, are you?
“S-stop! What do you think you’re doing to Malty!”

“You share the same guilt, indeed. You brought baseless accusations and interference to a sacred duel. Even if I were to cut you down here with the authority of a Hero, I doubt any nation would object.”

Father’s arguments, as Shield Hero, carried no weight here, but mine, as Spear Hero, held at least some authority even as an adversary. And above all, given how blatantly he’d caused a scene, there was no room left for excuses.
“Itsuki, what will it be? You’re fine with calling this a loss too, yes?”
“Ugh… f-fine… those people over there did something needless. Let’s… just stop this, this time.”
Well, well. How wonderful that pain had made Itsuki so agreeable. However, it seemed the shock had caused him to lose consciousness. Father tended to him and laid him down to rest right there.
“Then I trust we can agree the match goes to Father.”
“I would never permit such a thing—”
“Itsuki admitted defeat before losing consciousness. If that’s not convincing enough for you, shall I call for Ren?”
“I saw… everything. So this is how it ends, after all that fuss about a proper duel.”
Ren came stumbling over, none too steady on his feet.
“You people… enough already. Because of you, Itsuki suffered something far worse than simple defeat—it was humiliation.”
“Grr…”
“Buh…”

Trash and the Crimson Swine groaned in frustration. Looking at the results, Father’s strategy really was impressive. He’d used the Crimson Swine’s interference against Itsuki, then turned Trash’s underhanded meddling right back at him by using Itsuki as a shield to deal massive damage. And on top of that, the outcome left Itsuki with absolutely no room for excuses.
“What an outrageous bunch.”
Ren, clearly irritated, spat out words of contempt at Trash and his lot.
“…Well then, as promised, I’ll be taking my reward.”
Father approached Trash and Ren, who stood glaring at each other, and stated flatly.
“Grrrnn…”

“Ah, having Knight Éclair-san as the reward is fine. I don’t need the wave bounty anymore. And I have no intention of coming to the castle again. But the next time you people pull something like this… I won’t hold back anymore, understand?”
Father then turned a look of contempt toward the Crimson Swine as well.
“What a repulsive creature. Rotten to the core, through and through… I’ve never met anyone this disgusting before.”
“B-bhee! Bhee-hyaaaaaaaaa!”
The Crimson Swine let out an enraged squeal, but the moment Ren also pointed his sword at it, it snapped back to its senses and started muttering some kind of excuse.
“Hmph… not worth listening to. Just get out of our sight already.”
“Bh… Bhee-hyaaaa!”

Ignoring the hysterically screeching Crimson Swine, Father and Ren walked away. Even the soldiers, apparently realizing that any further interference would cost them their lives, stood staring blankly at Father and the others rather than at Trash and the Crimson Swine.
“Wow… so cool.”
At that, Kuro-chan’s eyes sparkled at Ren’s attitude, and he tried to approach. Ren immediately darted behind Father as if to hide from him.
“Ahaha… Kuro-chan, we’re heading back now, so say your goodbyes to Ren. Everyone, time to go home!”
“Aww… but when darkness once again covers all, fate shall bring us together once more—”
“Well then, time to withdraw! Everyone, let’s head home!”
“““Yes, ma’am!”””
And so, we began preparing to leave. Ah, we decided to have Filolial-sama carry off Crocodile Guy in his Demi-Human form.
“I wondered what would happen if I tried this, but things turned out even more hostile than I expected… I’m honestly not sure anymore whether I can grant Raphtalia-chan and the others’ wish.”

Muttering something about how it seemed like some strange faction was bound to interfere again but that he’d manage somehow, Father led us down to the underground prison, all the way to Éclair’s cell.
“Boo.”
Hey, Lazy Pig! How long do you intend to keep filming, I say! Don’t you dare follow us!
